mainTopic: When worship makes an animal a forbidden נעבד: forced worship, a friend's animal, and acts done on the animal itself
overview: First, חזקיה brings a פסוק showing that idolatrous items lose their status only when they are smashed like crumbling limestone. Then a ברייתא teaches that a person can make his own item a forbidden נעבד, but not his friend's. Another ברייתא counts worship done 'באונס' (under force), and the גמרא asks whether that means grabbing a friend's animal. רמי בר חמא answers that the person was forced to bow to his own animal. רבי זירא objects that the Torah frees someone who acts under force. רבא answers that force frees a person only in private, while forced worship in public still counts. The רבנן offer רבא support from platforms used during a time of persecution, but he turns it down. חזקיה and רב אדא בר אהבה then give other answers about a friend's animal, and the conclusion is that doing an act on it, like pouring wine between its horns or cutting one סימן, makes it forbidden. Finally, the גמרא looks for the source of this rule and pushes away two suggestions, the כהנים and the מזבח stones. The search for a source continues on the next amud.

steps.title: חזקיה's verse: idolatrous items lose their status only when smashed
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה brings a פסוק in ישעיהו as the source for the rule just discussed: idolatrous items lose their status only when they are smashed like crumbling limestone.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: What is the source? The פסוק says: 'When he makes all the altar stones like crushed limestone, the אשרים and sun-images will not rise.' If they are like crushed limestone, the אשרים and sun-images will not rise. If not, they will rise.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה gives the פסוק behind the rule being discussed: an idolatrous item loses its forbidden status only when it is smashed to pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the פסוק as a condition. If the stones are smashed like limestone, the idolatry 'will not rise', meaning its status is gone. If they are not smashed, it 'will rise', meaning it stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the verse? (asking for the Torah source)
limestone or chalk stones, which crumble easily

phrases.english: חזקיה said: What is the verse?
'When he makes all the stones of the altar
like limestones that are crushed to pieces,
the אשרים and sun-images will not rise.'
If there is 'like crushed limestones',
then the אשרים and sun-images will not rise;
if not, they will rise.
phrases.notes: 'Rise' means they keep their idol status and stay forbidden.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: An idolatrous item loses its status only when it is smashed like crumbling limestone, as learned from ישעיהו 27:9.
steps.whatToRemember: Smashing to pieces is what removes the status of idolatry. Without that, the item stays forbidden.

steps.title: A ברייתא: you can forbid only your own animal by worshipping it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that an item a person worshipped becomes forbidden if it belongs to him, but not if it belongs to someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: If a person worshipped his own item, it is forbidden. If he worshipped his friend's item, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. A person cannot make his friend's property forbidden by worshipping it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets the base rule for the rest of this section. Making something a נעבד depends on ownership: a person can only forbid what is his.

keyTerms.meaning: an item, such as an animal, that was worshipped as an idol

phrases.english: It was taught: A worshipped item that is his own is forbidden,
but one belonging to his friend is permitted.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person's own worshipped item is forbidden. Another person's item that he worshipped stays permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is what the next ברייתא seems to contradict, and the rest of this section tries to settle that contradiction.

steps.title: Contradiction: 'worshipped under force' seems to mean a friend's animal
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says worship under אונס also creates a נעבד. The גמרא suggests this means grabbing a friend's animal, which would contradict the first ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here is a contradiction: What counts as a נעבד? Anything that people worship, whether by mistake or on purpose, whether by force or willingly. What is this case of 'force'? Isn't it where someone forcibly took his friend's animal and bowed to it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that seems to clash with the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second ברייתא includes worship 'באונס' (by force). The גמרא suggests that 'force' means taking a friend's animal by force and worshipping it. If so, a friend's animal can become forbidden, which goes against step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction
What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: And here is a contradiction: What is a worshipped item?
phrases.notes: This ברייתא is about an animal that can no longer be brought as a קרבן because it was worshipped.

phrases.english: Anything that people worship,
whether by mistake or on purpose,
whether by force or willingly.
This case of 'force': what is it like?
Isn't it where he forcibly took his friend's animal
and bowed down to it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא of step 2 using another ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that worshipping a friend's item does not forbid it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'worship under force' means taking a friend's animal by force, then a friend's animal can become a נעבד, which contradicts step 2.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'force' is first read as the worshipper forcing the animal away from its owner, not as someone forcing the worshipper. The next step switches to the second meaning.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: the person himself was forced to bow to his own animal
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא explains that 'force' means non-Jews forced the person to bow to his own animal, so there is no contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: No. It is a case where non-Jews forced him, and he bowed to his own animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא answers the contradiction by reading 'force' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his reading, the person being forced is the worshipper, not the animal's owner. The animal is his own, so the first ברייתא's rule about a friend's animal stays in place.

phrases.english: רמי בר חמא said: No,
it is a case where non-Jews forced him
and he bowed down to his very own animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the case: the worshipper was forced, and the animal was his own.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Force' means the worshipper himself was forced to bow to his own animal.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the Torah frees someone who acts under force
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא objects that the Torah frees a person who acts under אונס, so forced worship should not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא challenged this: The Torah frees someone who acted under force, as it is written: 'And to the girl you shall do nothing.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא attacks רמי בר חמא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the worshipper was forced, the Torah treats him as not guilty, just as it frees the girl in the פסוק who was forced. So how could his forced bowing count as real worship and make the animal a נעבד?

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One, meaning the Torah
frees him from guilt or punishment

phrases.english: רבי זירא challenged it:
The Torah frees one who acts under force,
as it is written: 'And to the girl you shall do nothing'!
phrases.notes: דברים 22:26. This is the engaged girl who was attacked by force.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רמי בר חמא's answer in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's reading that forced worship of one's own animal makes it a נעבד.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah frees a person who acts under אונס, so his forced bowing should not count as worship at all.

steps.title: רבא: 'and live by them' removes forced worship from the prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a source that speaks about idol worship directly: לא תעבדם covered everything, but וחי בהם removed the case of אונס.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Everything was included in 'you shall not serve them.' But when the פסוק spelled out 'and live by them,' and not die by them, the case of force was taken out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins a new answer to רבי זירא's objection. First he shows from the פסוקים that, in general, worship under force is taken out of the prohibition. The next step adds an important limit to this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לא תעבדם would have included even forced worship. But וחי בהם teaches that a person should live by the מצוות, not die for them, so אונס is taken out. This is only the first half of רבא's answer; in the next step he shows that the exclusion has a limit.

keyTerms.meaning: you shall not serve them (the idols)
and he shall live by them

phrases.english: Rather, רבא said:
All cases were included in 'you shall not serve them,'
and when the verse spelled out for you 'and live by them,'
and not that he should die by them,
the case of force was taken out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: הַכֹּל הָיוּ בִּכְלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins רבא's answer to רבי זירא's objection in step 5. Step 7 completes it.
steps.whatToRemember: לא תעבדם includes all idol worship, but וחי בהם takes out the case of אונס.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic source for the idea that a person forced to commit an עבירה is treated differently from one who acts willingly.

steps.title: Private Force Versus Public Force
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a second פסוק, ולא תחללו את שם קדשי, which forbids worship even under אונס. He settles the clash with וחי בהם: וחי בהם covers private worship, and ולא תחללו covers public worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then the Torah wrote, 'And you shall not profane My holy name,' which means it is forbidden even under force. How do these fit together? One פסוק is about private, and the other is about public.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes the derivation he began in the last step. He brings a פסוק that seems to clash with וחי בהם and then shows how the two fit together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: וחי בהם said a forced person is free. ולא תחללו says forced worship is still forbidden. רבא splits them by setting: in private, force frees you, but in public, worship is a חילול ה׳ even under force.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall not profane My holy name': the source for חילול ה׳
'How so?': how do two sources that seem to clash fit together

steps.whatToRemember: In private, force frees a person from idol worship. In public, it does not, because public worship is a חילול ה׳. So an animal worshipped under force in public becomes forbidden.
steps.whyThisMatters: This private/public split is the basis for the famous rule of when a person must give up his life rather than worship idols.

phrases.english: And then the Merciful One wrote:
"And you shall not profane My holy name,"
meaning that it applies even under force.
How do these fit together?
This one is in private, and that one is in public.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is וחי בהם (force frees you). 'That one' is ולא תחללו (still forbidden).

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא כֵּיצַד? הָא בְּצִנְעָא, וְהָא בְּפַרְהֶסְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's answer from step 6 by adding a second פסוק and reconciling the two. This answers רבי זירא's objection in step 5: forced worship done in public still counts, so רמי בר חמא's case and the ברייתא's 'באונס' both stand.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two פסוקים apply to different settings (private vs. public).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: וחי בהם alone suggests that force always frees a person, so forced worship never counts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Force frees a person only in private. Forced worship in public still counts and makes the object forbidden.

steps.title: The רבנן Bring Support from the Platforms Teaching
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן bring a ברייתא for רבא: platforms that non-Jews used during a time of persecution stay forbidden even after the persecution ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רבא: A ברייתא supports you. Platforms of non-Jews from a time of persecution stay forbidden, even after the persecution is over.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן offer רבא a proof that forced worship can still make something forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During a שמד, Jews were forced to worship on these platforms, yet the platforms stay forbidden. That looks just like רבא's rule that forced worship, in the right setting, still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A ברייתא is taught that supports you'
Platforms or bases used in idol worship
A time of persecution, when the rulers forced Jews to give up their religion

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rava:
A ברייתא is taught that supports you:
Platforms of non-Jews
from a time of persecution:
even though the persecution ended,
those platforms do not lose their status.
phrases.notes: He means the platforms stay forbidden even though the persecution is over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רבא's conclusion in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that forced worship can still make an object forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about platforms used during a time of persecution that stay forbidden afterward.

steps.title: רבא Turns Down the Support
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ברייתא does not prove his point. Maybe a Jew who had left the faith worshipped there willingly, and that is why the platforms are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: If you mean because of this, it does not support me. Say that there was an apostate Jew who worshipped it willingly.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא refuses the proof the רבנן offered him, even though it would have helped his own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works only if the platforms became forbidden through forced worship. רבא points out another possible reason: a willing worshipper, a ישראל משומד. So the ברייתא does not have to be about forced worship at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jew who has left the faith (an apostate)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't be surprised that רבא rejects a proof for his own view. The גמרא wants honest proofs, and a proof that can be explained another way proves nothing.

phrases.english: He said to them:
If it is because of this, it does not support me,
say that there was an apostate Jew
and he worshipped it willingly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. רבא's rule itself still stands.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The platforms may have become forbidden through a willing apostate's worship, not through forced worship.

steps.title: רב אשי: It Was Certainly an Apostate
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי strengthens רבא's rejection. It is not just a possibility; it is certain that a willing apostate worshipped there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Don't say 'say' as if it were only a maybe. Rather, there certainly was an apostate Jew who worshipped it willingly.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adjusts the wording of רבא's answer. He turns 'maybe' into 'certainly.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא only showed that the ברייתא could be read another way. רב אשי holds that this other reading is the only correct one, so the ברייתא is definitely about willing worship and gives no support at all for forced worship.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Do not say "say,"
phrases.notes: He means: don't present it as only a maybe, the way רבא's word 'say' did.

phrases.english: rather, there certainly was an apostate Jew
and he worshipped it willingly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens רבא's rejection in step 9 from a possibility to a certainty.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully removes the ברייתא as support for רבא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא is definitely about willing worship, not forced worship.

steps.title: חזקיה's Answer: Wine Poured on the Animal's Horns
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה gives a new answer to the contradiction from step 3. The ברייתא that forbids someone else's animal is talking about pouring wine as an offering onto its horns.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: For example, where someone poured wine onto its horns as an offering to an idol.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the original clash between the two ברייתות and brings a different answer from רמי בר חמא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא said the person bowed to his own animal. חזקיה keeps the case of a friend's animal. He says it becomes forbidden because an act of worship, a wine offering, was done right on the animal itself.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For example' or 'such as': it introduces the exact case

phrases.english: Chizkiya said:
phrases.notes: He is answering the clash from step 3, about worshipping a friend's animal.

phrases.english: for example, where he poured, as an offering to an idol,
wine onto its horns.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the private/public discussion and gives a different answer to the contradiction from step 3, instead of רמי בר חמא's answer in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the case: the animal belonged to someone else, but worship was done directly on it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second ברייתא seems to say that worshipping a friend's animal forbids it, against the first ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Plain worship of a friend's animal does not forbid it. Pouring a wine offering on its horns does.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: That Is Just a Platform
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה objects to חזקיה. An animal that wine was poured on was not itself worshipped. It is only a platform for the offering, and so it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה challenged this: Is this something that was worshipped? This is just a platform, and it is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה attacks חזקיה's answer from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pouring wine on the animal does not make the animal the object of worship. The animal just holds the offering, like a base or altar. A platform like this, belonging to someone else, stays permitted, so חזקיה's case cannot explain why the animal is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Challenges it': a strong objection to what was just said
Something that was itself worshipped, which makes it forbidden

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava challenged this:
Is this something that was worshipped?
This is merely a platform,
phrases.notes: The animal just holds the wine offering, like a base, instead of being worshipped itself.

phrases.english: and it is permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.kashyaTarget: חזקיה's case of wine poured on a friend's animal's horns.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pouring wine on the animal makes it only a platform, not an object of worship. A platform stays permitted, so the animal should not be forbidden.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: wine poured between the horns
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה explains that the ברייתא is talking about pouring wine between the animal's horns. That is a real act done on the animal itself, so it becomes forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אדא בר אהבה said: The case is where he poured wine for the idol between the animal's horns. Since he did an act on the animal, it becomes forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה gives his own answer to the contradiction from step 3, after he rejected חזקיה's answer in step 12.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 12 the worry was that the animal was only a stand for the offering. Now the point is different: pouring wine right between its horns is an act done on the animal's own body. Bowing to someone else's animal does nothing, but doing an act on it makes it forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: he did an act on it

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Adda bar Ahava said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁנִּיסֵּךְ לָהּ יַיִן בֵּין קַרְנֶיהָ,
phrases.english: For example, where he poured wine to it between its horns,
phrases.notes: "To it" means as worship of the animal, as an offering.

phrases.english: since he did an act on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting חזקיה's answer in step 12, רב אדא בר אהבה offers his own version of the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Pouring wine on the animal makes it only a stand for the offering, so the animal stays permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Pouring the wine between its horns is an act done on the animal itself, so the animal becomes forbidden even though it belongs to someone else.

steps.title: Support from עולא quoting רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: עולא brings רבי יוחנן's rule: bowing to another person's animal does not make it forbidden, but doing an act on it does.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what עולא said when he came, in the name of רבי יוחנן: Even though they said that bowing to someone else's animal does not make it forbidden, if he did an act on it, he made it forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב אדא בר אהבה's answer with a rule from רבי יוחנן that עולא brought from ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן makes the same split that רב אדא used. Bowing alone is just an attitude toward the animal and cannot forbid what is not yours. A physical act of worship done on the animal itself does forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: one who bows down in worship

phrases.english: And this is like that which, when Ulla came,
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even though they said
that one who bows to another's animal did not make it forbidden,
if he did an act on it, he made it forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הָא דַּאֲתָא עוּלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 13 by showing that רבי יוחנן taught the same principle.
steps.raayaObject: רב אדא בר אהבה's claim that doing an act on another person's animal makes it forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's statement, brought by עולא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main rule for the rest of the sugya: bowing alone does not forbid another person's animal, but an act done on it does.

steps.title: רב נחמן: רב הונא already taught this in Bavel
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says עולא's rule is nothing new. רב הונא already taught that cutting one סימן of another person's animal in front of an idol makes it forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to them: Go out and tell עולא that רב הונא already explained your teaching in בבל. רב הונא said: If someone else's animal was lying in front of an idol, once he cut one סימן, he made it forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן points out that the idea עולא brought from ארץ ישראל was already known in בבל through רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's case is a clear example of 'doing an act': slaughtering, even only partly, in front of an idol. Cutting just one סימן is already enough of an act to forbid an animal that belongs to someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: one of the two pipes cut in שחיטה: the windpipe or the food pipe

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to them:
Go out and say to Ulla:

phrases.aramaic: כְּבָר תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַב הוּנָא לִשְׁמַעְתָּיךְ בְּבָבֶל,
phrases.english: Rav Huna already explained your teaching in Babylonia,
as Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: הָיְתָה בֶּהֱמַת חֲבֵירוֹ רְבוּצָה בִּפְנֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
phrases.english: If another person's animal was lying before an idol,

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן שֶׁשָּׁחַט בָּהּ סִימָן אֶחָד — אֲסָרָהּ.
phrases.english: once he cut one siman in it, he made it forbidden.
phrases.notes: Cutting even one of the two pipes already counts as doing an act of worship on the animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב נַחְמָן פּוּקוּ וֶאֱמַרוּ לֵיהּ לְעוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that עולא's rule from step 14 was already taught by רב הונא in בבל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cutting one סימן of another person's animal in front of an idol makes the animal forbidden.

steps.title: What is the source for this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that an act can forbid another person's animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that he makes it forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule from steps 13 to 15. This sets up the next two steps, where possible sources are tried and rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a person cannot make forbidden something that does not belong to him. So the גמרא wants a source showing that an act of worship can forbid someone else's property.

phrases.english: From where do we know that he made it forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule from steps 14 and 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that doing an act of worship forbids an animal that belongs to someone else.

steps.title: Priests are not a good source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning the rule from כהנים who served an idol, then rejects it. כהנים are people with understanding, so they are a different case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say we learn it from כהנים, maybe כהנים are different, because they are people with understanding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first source, כהנים, and immediately pushes it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן who served an idol is disqualified from serving in the בית המקדש. But a כהן is a thinking person who is responsible for what he does. An animal has no understanding, so the case of כהנים cannot teach us about another person's animal.

phrases.english: If you say it is from the priests,
phrases.notes: This means כהנים who served an idol and are then not allowed to serve in the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: but perhaps priests are different,
since they are people with understanding!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes and rejects a first answer to the question in step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning the rule from כהנים.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: כהנים have understanding and are responsible for their actions. An animal does not, so the cases are not alike.

steps.title: The altar stones are not a good source either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning the rule from the מזבח stones that the Greeks made forbidden, then rejects it because of רב פפא's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, maybe we learn it from the stones of the מזבח. But maybe that case is explained like רב פפא said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second source, the מזבח stones, and pushes that one away too. The search for a source continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Greeks made the מזבח stones forbidden even though the stones were not theirs. But רב פפא explained that when they entered the בית המקדש, it became their property. So that case is about their own property and teaches nothing about another person's animal.

phrases.english: Rather, it is from the stones of the altar,
phrases.notes: These are the stones the Greeks made forbidden when they entered the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: but perhaps it is as Rav Pappa said?
phrases.notes: רב פפא said earlier (52b) that when the Greeks entered, the בית המקדש became theirs, so the stones were their own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the כהנים source fails in step 17, a second source is proposed and rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning the rule from the מזבח stones.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: According to רב פפא, the stones became the Greeks' own property, so that case does not show that a person can forbid someone else's property.
